subject: Sandbox activation + SDK routing commitments
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Collins <sofia.collins@finerva.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: sandbox activation items + next steps

Hi Sofia — thanks again for the conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before we hand off to engineering: 

Summary of needs from the call:
- Finerva wants a 2-week sandbox trial to validate transaction enrichment and entity resolution at ~100 TPS peak, with streaming inference for realtime scoring.
- Security requirement: data must be sent to Redwood hosted sandbox with tokenized test data, audit logs retained for 30 days.
- Integration preferences: use our Python SDK for streaming routes, with a fallback to REST generate endpoint for batch backfills.

Success criteria (proposed):
1) End-to-end latency under 150ms 95th pct for streaming route under 100 TPS
2) Sampled accuracy measured by Finerva’s internal eval set: recall >= 92% for entity matches
3) End-to-end traceability: request_id mapping in Finerva logs and Redwood trace links

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): share POC proposal and integration checklist (attached)
- Week 1: sandbox access + SDK onboarding; quick smoke test of streaming route
- Week 2: run acceptance harness and collect metrics; finalize success gating

Ownership suggestion:
- Finerva: Marco (engineering lead) — integration work and test data
- Redwood: Aditya (solutions engineer) — SDK routing and streaming setup; Ben (AE) — commercial/credits coordination

Attachments: redwood-poc-proposal.pdf, integration-checklist.xlsx (high level scope + per-route tasks)

Would you like us to kick off sandbox access on Monday? If yes, Aditya will open the sandbox and share credentials + example SDK snippet.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Collins <sofia.collins@finerva.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Rivera <marco.rivera@finerva.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Recap: sandbox activation items + next steps

Neha — thanks for the clear recap. Confirmed: we want to proceed. A few clarifying items from our side before sandbox access:

1) Dataset: we will provide tokenized subset (~50k rows) by Monday. Will Redwoods accept CSV with hashed PII?
2) SDK support: our infra is Python (FastAPI). We prefer streaming over websocket-based SDK if possible; can you confirm the streaming transport (websocket vs HTTP/2) and sample snippet?
3) Metrics: can Redwood surface cost estimates for the expected throughput so our finance partner can sign off on the trial?

We’ll block Marco to work with Aditya once you provision the sandbox. Monday activation sounds good.

—Sofia
Sofia Collins
Head of Data Products, Finerva
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Finerva sandbox kickoff plan + action items (do not forward)

Team — looped in Grace for instrumentation/acceptance gating. Action items below so we can hit Week 1 goals: 

Aditya:
- Provision sandbox tenant for Finerva with VPC-restricted endpoint and 30-day audit log retention; share creds and an allowlist for Finerva IPs by Monday 07/31.
- Provide a Python streaming SDK example for FastAPI using HTTP/2 server push (or websocket fallback) and a small snippet that shows request_id propagation. Add the sdk-route-reference.md to the drive folder.
- Configure automatic prefix caching for entity lookup route and set batching threshold to preserve latency SLOs.

Grace:
- Create an acceptance harness (script + sample dataset) to measure latency and accuracy; include 95th and P50 metrics and an automated report to upload to the shared Drive.

Ben:
- Confirm trial credit allocation and confirm commercial touchpoints (we agreed 2 weeks, include optional +1 week extension if integration blocker).

Sofia / Finerva asks that we confirm streaming protocol and cost estimate for 100 TPS peak. Aditya — can you produce a back-of-envelope cost delta for that workload (vCPU/GPU equivalent and estimated token units) when you provision the tenant?

I’m targeting sandbox activation Monday 07/31 so Marco can start smoke testing. Let me know if anything blocks.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Sofia Collins <sofia.collins@finerva.com>, Marco Rivera <marco.rivera@finerva.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: sandbox activation items + next steps

Hi all — sandbox tenant is live and credentials are uploaded to the Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-poc-docs (see file "sandbox-credentials.txt"). Quick notes and attachments: 

- Attachments added: sdk-route-reference.md (Python FastAPI examples for HTTP/2 streaming + websocket fallback), quick-cost-estimate.xlsx (rough estimate for 100 TPS streaming), integration-checklist.xlsx (updated with owners).
- We accept CSV with hashed PII; Grace and I validated the acceptance harness against a small sample and saw ~120ms P95 on our internal sim for the streaming route with the cache on.
- Cost note: rough token-model mapping attached; bottom line is ~X credits/day at steady 100 TPS (see quick-cost-estimate.xlsx). Ben — please confirm credit allocation.

Next steps for Finerva (Marco/Sofia):
- Marco to run smoke tests and share the first test run logs by EOD Thursday 08/05.
- Sofia to confirm any additional security evidence or SOC-related artifacts required for the tenant (if yes, Ben will coordinate procurement docs).

Happy to jump on a quick debug call once Marco has the first run.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
